title: NFV
what: Network function virtualization where routers, firewalls, and load balancers run as software functions.
why: To reduce hardware dependence, increase flexibility, and improve scaling.
when: When network services must scale dynamically and move between resources.
example: A firewall instance deployed in a virtual environment instead of a dedicated appliance.

title: VNF
why: To run network features in software on a shared resource pool.
when: When service functions need placement, failover, or elastic scaling.

title: Service Chain
what: An ordered sequence of VNFs that traffic passes through.
why: To enforce security, optimization, and processing steps in a repeatable way.
when: When multiple network services must be applied in sequence.
example: Traffic passes through a vFirewall then a vLoadBalancer and then a vIDS.
